note: Clean pass with one real caveat about the WORDING, not the mapping. The only item text the study ever published is the SPSS variable labels in its S1 File, and those labels are DAMAGED WINDOWS of the original wording: they are capped at 70 characters (7 labels sit exactly at 70 and end mid-word -- NOTWORRY '...kept in their personn', WORKLONG '...than is best for patie', INFORMAT '...during shift c') and they are also cut on the LEFT, so 21 of 42 begin with the tail of a word plus a full stop ('fied. Patient safety is never sacrificed', 'ted. When an event is reported...', '. procedures and systems are good') and others simply start mid-sentence (GETSBUSY 'one area in this unit gets really busy others helpout'; EVALUATE 'we evaluate their effectiveness faster'). The labels are shipped EXACTLY as the file stores them -- all lowercase where the file is lowercase, artifacts and truncations left in place, nothing tidied and nothing padded. Canonical AHRQ HSOPSC wording was deliberately NOT substituted, because this administration is not canonical: 18 of the 42 labels are NEGATED rewrites of AHRQ's reverse-worded items ('Staff in this unit does not work longer hours than is best for patient care' against AHRQ A5 'Staff in this unit work longer hours...'), and the data run in the labels' direction, not AHRQ's -- all 18 correlate POSITIVELY (+0.128 to +0.548) with the 24 canonically-positive items' mean, where canonical polarity would make them negative. Substituting AHRQ text would therefore have shipped 18 items with their sense inverted relative to the responses. The paper (10.1371/journal.pone.0245966) reproduces no item wording at all: its Table 3 is dimension-level (12 dimensions, 42 items) and Tables 1-2 are demographics; S1 (the .sav) is the article's only Supporting Information file. instructions and section_prompt left NA for the same reason -- no administered instruction text is recoverable. Rights: the shipped wording is the study's own modified rendering, taken from a CC BY 4.0 PLOS deposit, and no restriction on the AHRQ instrument was quotable (ahrq.gov/sops/surveys/hospital/index.html returned 403 to a plain fetch and served only navigation chrome, no rights statement, on retry with a browser UA; sha256 of the retrieved page 3e39a7cdc56c989e942630ef5958c80aaec198f665f17826dbf91c2d6aaf53d1) -- no quote, so the rights rule does not fire. SEPARATE RESPONSE-DATA OBSERVATION, not an item-text issue and already flagged from the sibling table's batch_013 provenance: the S1 file carries a periodic exact-duplicate structure, and it lands on this table -- the full 42-item response pattern repeats exactly at lag 130 for 31.0% of rows, giving 270 distinct patterns across 411 respondents, which cannot happen by chance for 42 simultaneous values. Section 6 of the verify script reproduces it. Not raised with Ben by this round; batch_013 recorded that Xingyi was reviewing it.

Organizzazioni Speciali / Giunti Psychometrics 2004; internal locus of control, 6 items (d_6_3,12,16,22,26,33; prefix 'Loc I' numbered 2,5,6,8,9,11 -- gappy, i.e. the ORIGINAL instrument's item numbers), cited to ref [83] = Argentero & Vidotto, LOC-L, Mediatest 1994; and self-regulation, 8 reverse-worded items (d_6_7,10,14,18,24,28,31,34; prefix 'SeReg _R_' numbered 3,4,5,6,8,9,10,11), adapted from Grasmick et al. (1993) and Tangney et al. (2004). Extraction itself was fully solved before the rights check: the S3 SPSS file (journals.plos.org/plosone/article/file?type=supplementary&id=10.1371/journal.pone.0199924.s003, sha256 of the fetched file recorded in .cache) labels every d_6_N column, the processing script data/molino_2018_entrepreneurial_intention.py uses those column names verbatim as the IRW item codes (no positional assignment), and the S2 Questionnaire (Italian, administered) and S1 Questionnaire (English, authors' own translation) each print all 34 items numbered 1-34 matching d_6_1..d_6_34 exactly, with instructions 'Riflettendo su di te, indica il tuo grado di accordo rispetto alle seguenti affermazioni. (1 = per niente d'accordo; 7 = del tutto d'accordo)' and endpoint-only anchors at 1 and 7. So this is a data_labels mapping with an administered-Italian + study-supplied-English pair available -- nothing about access or ambiguity stopped it. Clean pass, two disclosed deviations. (1) 'pot' = the paper's 7 Passage-of-Time (PoT) judgment questions, not a named instrument; the table name is correct. (2) The study was administered in French (paper booklet, Clermont-Ferrand sample, French ethics committee; the S1 Table's STI columns are French). No French wording for the PoT questions exists in the deposit (S1 Table is the only supplement and carries column headers only) or in the paper, so the paper's own English rendering ships in the base fields with language=French and no _translated columns -- the documented fallback. (3) The paper gives the seven questions as two compound sentences with bracketed lists; each item_text expands its own branch into a full question (e.g. 'Do you think that time passes fast (1) now, (2) this week...' -> 'Do you think that time passes fast this week?'). No words added beyond the shared stem. (4) Only scale endpoints are labelled (1 'not at all', 7 'a lot'); points 2-6 ship blank option_text rather than padded. (5) No literal instruction text is published, so instructions is NA. Rights: ad-hoc PoT questions from the Droit-Volet research line, reproduced in a CC BY 4.0 PLOS ONE article; no fee, permission, NC, ND or no-redistribution clause locatable for the wording, and nothing in instrument_rights_register.csv matches.
